title: No registry every lane must edit: size-ratchet allowances stop being one shared file
summary: From the inbox architecture review (N3). go/internal/sizeratchet/offenders.json holds 283 exact-match allowances across 93 packages, and the ratchet refuses a shrunk function whose allowance was not lowered, so every change to a listed function edits the one file (9 commits in four hours on 2026-09-28). Two lanes that both touch it never carry an audited verdict across a rebase (treedelta is full-index): cycle 1731 re-authored after cycle 1732 for this reason. rawgitratchet/baseline.json has the same shape. The review's interim step (declare offenders.json in every pending shrink item so the planner never co-schedules two) is not taken: it would serialize the only lane-ready supply, and a co-scheduled shrink costs a re-author and a re-audit, never a FAIL.
acceptance: Two lanes that change listed functions in different packages touch disjoint files: the allowance lives beside its package, or shrinking is allowed (ceiling semantics) and a deterministic tighten step runs at the wave boundary
A rebase of one such lane over the other is proven identical by treedelta.Identical (test)
Both ratchets still refuse growth past the allowance and a new offender
fix: Partly resolved 2026-09-28 (fix/sizeratchet-is-a-ceiling): an allowance is now a ceiling, so no lane needs to write offenders.json to pass (shrinks and stale entries are slack); the remaining work is the single writer: a boundary `evolve sizeratchet tighten` (pure Tighten + a byte-stable Encode; json.MarshalIndent(m, "", "  ") + "\n" reproduces today's file) and a build-floor no-growth check against the base (commentaudit.ReadAtBase pattern), then one exported offenders path constant (today written three ways) and one 50-line cap (test/structure/limits.go duplicates it with >=).
